ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The mRNA sequence at the top of the figure is shown by triplets as AUG CCA CUA GCA CGU; the corresponding protein band below it is labeled Met-Pro-Leu-Ala-Arg, that is, methionine-proline-leucine-alanine-arginine. The figure also gives a genetic code table, from which it can be found that AUG corresponds to methionine, CCA corresponds to proline, CAG corresponds to glutamine, and CAC corresponds to histidine. Reasoning: The question states that after methionine has already been translated, one uracil in the mRNA is deleted, so the first codon AUG remains unchanged. The original sequence after AUG is CCA CUA GCA CGU; after deleting the U in CUA, the subsequent bases are regrouped by triplets as CCA CAG CAC .... So the new codons are read as AUG | CCA | CAG | CAC, corresponding to the amino acids methionine-proline-glutamine-histidine.

raw_record.question_text: What is the resulting amino acid sequence if a mutation deletes a uracil from the messenger RNA after methionine is translated?

method.method_draft: Read the mRNA letters in the image as AUG CCA CUA GCA CGU and note the protein strip below it as Met-Pro-Leu-Ala-Arg. The question says a uracil is deleted after methionine, so the first codon AUG stays fixed and the next triplets are regrouped from the shifted sequence: AUG | CCA | CAG | CAC | ... Using the codon table in the image, AUG = Met, CCA = Pro, CAG = Gln, CAC = His, so the resulting sequence is Methionine–proline–glutamine–histidine.
